facts.caveat: The page does not say whether private land is covered.
facts.fact: Fly-tipping, dog fouling, dead animals, spillages, broken glass and other dangerous items seen on a road, pavement or public space in Southampton can be reported as a street cleaning problem.
facts.topic: What can be reported as street cleaning

facts.caveat: This is an aim, not a guarantee.
facts.fact: The council aims to deal with over 75% of urgent street cleaning requests within one working day of report.

facts.caveat: National limits can change. Re-check on the day.
facts.fact: The fixed penalty for fly-tipping is 400 pounds, reduced to 250 pounds if paid within ten days of the notice being issued.

facts.caveat: The page does not mention private land specifically.
facts.fact: The council defines fly-tipping as waste greater than one black sack left on land without the owner's permission.

facts.caveat: The page does not mention licensed waste carriers or transfer notes.
facts.fact: A fixed penalty can be issued to anyone who allows their waste to be fly-tipped. The page gives the example of using someone found online to dispose of waste without getting their full details and a receipt.
Private land or property fly-tipping must be resolved by the owner or occupier; form is for public land or witnessed fly-tips with evidence of who did it.

form_notes: Private land: owner/occupier resolves it. Report only if on public land, or witnessed with evidence of who did it.
